newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Cardenas sees rise in July-Sept coffee.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Cardenas sees rise in July-Sept coffee.

text.p: Jorge Cardenas, general manager of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, said he sees July-Sept coffee prices rising to somewhere around current spot May levels because of continuing supply jitters.
"It's expected that July and September prices will be improving to the level of May," Cardenas told reporters.
He did not elaborate, but the CSCE's key May/July switch, an indicator of near-term avaialability, widened to 23.85 in New York Monday.

In his remarks, Cardenas also said a shipment of 200,000 70-kg bags of coffee was delayed by the six-day strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union that ended with a negotiated settlement last Friday.
"It did a lot of damage to coffee flows," he said of the strike, adding that all coffee held up by the strike would be shipped to the country's three main ports this week.
